When solving an exercise at the end of [Chapter 1](../chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) or [Chapter 4](../chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), the chapter title itself hands you the primary mathematical invariant before you read a single line of the problem statement. In a live contest, **problems arrive completely untagged**. You are given a narrative about overlapping transmissions, symmetric partitions, or substring decompositions, along with numerical constraints ($N \le 5 \times 10^5$, $W \le 10^{18}$, or $Q \le 10^5$), and you must determine on your own which structural periodicity or border-compression mechanism governs the problem.

This checkpoint tests **blind diagnostic recognition** across all four chapters of Part I (`Ch 01`–`Ch 04`). None of the visible problem statements in Section 2 reveal which chapter or technique applies.

::: {.callout-important title="Zero-Spoiler Protocol & Progressive Hints"}

1. **Strict Zero-Spoiler Rule in Visible Statements**: Every problem statement (`CP-I-01` through `CP-I-07`) is written in pure contest form without naming the target chapter (`Ch 01`–`Ch 04`) or technique (`Fine–Wilf`, `Border AP`, `Modulo Shortest Path`, `slink DP`).
2. **Diagnose Before Peeking**: Before opening any dropdown on a problem, write down on scratch paper:
   - Which **Part I paradigm** (`Ch 01`–`Ch 04`) is triggered by the constraints and objective;
   - Which **lookalike decoy paradigm** must be ruled out, and why;
   - The **combinatorial word invariant** that collapses the naive $\Theta(N^2)$ or $\Theta(W)$ bottleneck.
3. **Four-Stage Progressive Unmasking**:
   - **Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination**: Explains how to identify the governing paradigm and rule out lookalike decoys purely from constraints and query semantics.
   - **Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant**: States the exact algebraic or periodicity identity needed for the reduction.
   - **Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly**: Outlines the state representation, transition order, and complexity target.
   - **Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution**: Full proof, boundary pitfall audit (`BP-1A-01` through `BP-1A-08`), and non-standard reference kernel where clarifying.
:::

## 1. Blind Diagnostic Triage Guide & Decoy Elimination

The most common strategic failure in Part I contest problems is **confusing two surface-similar periodicity or border patterns** that require completely different algorithmic machinery. Before attempting the seven blind problems below, study the two primary Part I **Decoy Pairs** and the decision flowchart.

### 1.1 Decoy Pair A: Simultaneous Period Intersection (`Ch 01`) vs. Sequential Overlap Semigroup (`Ch 03`)

Both paradigms involve a base length $N \le 5 \times 10^5$, periods $p = N - b$ derived from borders $b \in \operatorname{Border}(S)$, and often a huge length parameter $L, W \le 10^{18}$. How do you tell them apart in 30 seconds?

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 01` Paradigm (`T-1A-01`: Fine–Wilf & Orbit Counting) | `Ch 03` Paradigm (`T-1A-03`: Border-Group Modulo Shortest Path) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **How Periods Act on the Target Word** | **Simultaneous global or interval constraints**: the *same* word (or overlapping interval $I$) simultaneously satisfies $W[i] = W[i+p]$ **and** $W[i] = W[i+q]$ for all valid $i$. | **Sequential additive concatenation**: we place copies of $S$ one after another; the $t$-th transition chooses *one* border $b_t \in \operatorname{Border}(S)$ and advances total length by $+ (N - b_t)$. |
| **Governing Algebraic Object** | **Equivalence relation / Undirected orbit graph** on indices $\{1, \dots, L\}$ generated by edges $i \leftrightarrow i + p_k$. | **Additive semigroup / Frobenius knapsack** of subset sums $\sum_{t=1}^m (N - b_t)$ inside $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ modulo a dynamically chosen base period $x_k$. |
| **Behavior at Huge Length ($L, W \gg N$)** | Above threshold $L \ge p + q - \gcd(p, q)$, periods **collapse to a single period** $\gcd(p, q)$. Below threshold, orbit count is $p + q - L$. | Above the Frobenius number, achievable lengths become periodic **modulo $x_{\min}$**, governed by shortest paths $D[r]$ on residue cycles. |
| **Fatal Misdiagnosis** | Running shortest-path knapsack when the problem imposes *simultaneous* periods on a single string (which collapses to $\gcd$). | Replacing the set of available shift weights $\{N - b\}$ by their $\gcd$ immediately without paying the minimum reachability cost $D[r] \le W$! |

### 1.2 Decoy Pair B: Online Active-Border Maintenance (`Ch 02`) vs. Fixed-Left-Endpoint `slink` DP (`Ch 04`)

Both paradigms process a string $S[1..N]$ left-to-right ($r = 1, 2, \dots, N$), cannot afford walking the $\Theta(N)$-deep KMP or PAM fail chain at step $r$, and rely on $O(\log r)$ shortcut links (`slink[u]` or `anc[u]`). Yet using `Ch 04`'s rolling `g[u]` array on a `Ch 02` problem—or vice versa—produces an immediate wrong answer.

| Diagnostic Dimension | `Ch 02` Paradigm (`T-1A-02`: Active Border Deletion & AP Queries) | `Ch 04` Paradigm (`T-1A-04` / `T-1A-05`: Series-Link `g[u]` Shift-Overlap DP) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nature of the Transition Weight** | **Right-endpoint-coupled or path-dependent**: the weight of a border $b$ at step $r$ depends on a dynamic range property of $[r-b+1..r]$ (such as $\min_{k \in [r-b+1, r]} W[k]$) or on which borders survive character $S[r+1]$. | **Fixed-left-endpoint (or polynomial in $L = r - i$)**: the contribution from cutting a palindromic/border suffix of length $L$ at $r$ depends *only* on the prefix state $dp[i]$ at the invariant left endpoint $i = r - L$ (or $(r-i)^m dp[i]$). |
| **Why $\Theta(1)$ Work per AP Holds** | Either each border **dies at most once** when $S[b+1] \ne S[r]$ (skipped in $O(1)$ via `anc[u]`), or an AP $(x_k, d_k, c_k)$ is queried in closed form / dyadic IPM. | **Shift-Overlap Identity**: $\mathcal{I}(u, r) = \mathcal{I}(\operatorname{fail}[u], r - d) \sqcup \{r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - d\}$, so `g[fail[u]]` computed at $r - d$ already stores the exact sum over the first $k - 1$ left endpoints! |
| **Fatal Misdiagnosis** | Trying to maintain $\sum_{b} \min_{k \in [r-b+1, r]} W[k]$ inside `g[u] = g[fail[u]] + ...` (invalid because appending $W[r]$ mutates the suffix minimum of *all* active left endpoints simultaneously). | Maintaining an explicit `std::map` of all $\Theta(N)$ individual borders when `g[u]` can aggregate each AP block in $O(1)$ time via left-endpoint invariance. |

## 2. Unspoiled Blind Checkpoint Problems (`CP-I-01` – `CP-I-07`)

---

### Problem `CP-I-01` — Minimum Stamp Cover

You are given a string $S[1..N]$ over the lowercase English alphabet, where $1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$. You wish to manufacture a single rubber stamp carrying a string $T[1..L]$ of minimum possible length $L$. Using this stamp, you must be able to print $S[1..N]$ on an initially blank strip of length $N$ by pressing $T$ onto one or more (possibly overlapping) intervals $[i, i + L - 1] \subseteq [1, N]$ such that:

1. Every position $k \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ is covered by at least one stamp impression;
2. Whenever two stamp impressions overlap at position $k$, they print the exact same character $S[k]$ (so the final printed string is $S[1..N]$).

Find the minimum possible length $L$ of such a stamp $T$.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$, Time Limit $1.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination**: This is *not* a partition DP into disjoint blocks (`Ch 04`), nor is it building a huge string of length $W > N$ by arbitrary overlaps (`Ch 03`). We are covering a fixed string $S[1..N]$ using overlapping occurrences of a single pattern $T$.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Because $T$ must cover index $1$ (the left end of $S$) and index $N$ (the right end of $S$) without hanging outside $[1, N]$, $T$ must be **both a prefix and a suffix of $S[1..N]$**—that is, $T = S[1..L]$ where $L \in \operatorname{Border}(S) \cup \{N\}$. By induction, for every prefix $S[1..i]$, its shortest valid stamp $T_i = S[1..dp[i]]$ must lie on the KMP fail chain of $i$, restricting $dp[i]$ to at most two candidates: either $dp[\pi[i]]$ or $i$ itself!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Let $dp[i]$ be the minimum length of a stamp that covers prefix $S[1..i]$.
Since any stamp covering $S[1..i]$ must be a border of $S[1..i]$, and any nontrivial border of $S[1..i]$ is also a border of $S[1..\pi[i]]$ (and therefore covers $S[1..\pi[i]]$), any proper stamp for $S[1..i]$ must have length $\ge dp[\pi[i]]$. Moreover, since $S[1..dp[\pi[i]]]$ already covers $S[1..\pi[i]]$, if any proper border of $S[1..i]$ covers $S[1..i]$, then $S[1..dp[\pi[i]]]$ itself covers $S[1..i]$!

When does $x = dp[\pi[i]]$ cover $S[1..i]$? Since the suffix $S[i - \pi[i] + 1 .. i] = S[1..\pi[i]]$ is already covered by stamps of length $x$, $x$ covers $S[1..i]$ without leaving an uncovered gap before $i - \pi[i] + 1$ **if and only if** there exists an earlier prefix $j < i$ such that:
$$dp[j] = dp[\pi[i]] \quad \text{and} \quad j \ge i - \pi[i].$$
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Compute the KMP prefix array $\pi[1..N]$ of $S$ in $O(N)$ time.
2. Maintain an array `last_end[1..N]`, where `last_end[x]` stores the largest prefix index $j < i$ seen so far whose minimum stamp length is $dp[j] = x$.
3. Sweep $i = 1, 2, \dots, N$:
   - If $\pi[i] > 0$ and $\text{last\_end}[dp[\pi[i]]] \ge i - \pi[i]$, set $dp[i] = dp[\pi[i]]$.
   - Otherwise, set $dp[i] = i$.
   - Update $\text{last\_end}[dp[i]] = i$.
4. Output $dp[N]$ in $O(N)$ total time and $O(N)$ space.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-I-01"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 1](../chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) (`T-1A-01`: Period–Border Duality & KMP Fail-Tree Cover Invariant · `[POI XII] Szablon` / `Luogu P3426`)**.
- **Proof of the Two-Candidate Collapse ($dp[i] \in \{dp[\pi[i]], i\}$)**:
  Suppose a stamp $T = S[1..b]$ with $b < i$ covers $S[1..i]$. Because the rightmost impression of $T$ ends at $i$ and the leftmost starts at $1$, $b \in \operatorname{Border}(S[1..i])$, so $b \le \pi[i]$ and $b \in \operatorname{Border}(S[1..\pi[i]]) \cup \{\pi[i]\}$. Furthermore, every impression of $T$ that lies completely inside $[1, \pi[i]]$ (including the one ending at $\pi[i]$, which exists because the suffix $[i-\pi[i]+1..i]$ is identical to $[1..\pi[i]]$) covers $S[1..\pi[i]]$. Hence $T$ is a valid stamp for $S[1..\pi[i]]$, and by definition $x = dp[\pi[i]]$ is the shortest stamp covering $S[1..\pi[i]]$—so $x$ is itself a stamp of $T$, meaning every impression of $T$ can be replaced by impressions of $S[1..x]$!
  Conversely, $S[1..x]$ covers the suffix $S[i-\pi[i]+1..i]$ (since that suffix equals $S[1..\pi[i]]$). To cover all of $S[1..i]$ without a gap between the prefix impressions and the suffix $[i-\pi[i]+1..i]$, we need an impression of $S[1..x]$ ending at some $j \in [i - \pi[i], i - 1]$. Such an impression exists (and connects back to index $1$ without gaps) iff $S[1..x]$ covers $S[1..j]$, which by minimality of $x$ is equivalent to $dp[j] = x$ for some $j \ge i - \pi[i]$.

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit**:
  - **Testing `last_end[x] >= i - x` instead of `last_end[x] >= i - pi[i]`**: This is the classic implementation bug. The entire suffix $S[i - \pi[i] + 1 .. i]$ of length $\pi[i] \ge x$ is *already* covered by $S[1..x]$ because $x = dp[\pi[i]]$ covers $S[1..\pi[i]]$. Thus the previous covered prefix $j$ only needs to reach $i - \pi[i]$, not $i - x$!
- **Complexity**: $O(N)$ time and $O(N)$ space.
::::

---

### Problem `CP-I-02` — Tandem-Repeat Necklace Prefixes

Given a string $S[1..N]$ of lowercase letters and a positive integer $K$ ($1 \le N, K \le 10^6$), we say that a prefix $S[1..i]$ has a **$(K, A, B)$-necklace decomposition** if there exist two (possibly empty) strings $A$ and $B$ such that:
$$S[1..i] = \underbrace{A B \, A B \, \dots \, A B}_{K \text{ times}} A = (AB)^K A.$$
For every prefix length $i \in \{1, 2, \dots, N\}$, output `1` if $S[1..i]$ admits at least one valid $(K, A, B)$-necklace decomposition, and `0` otherwise.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N, K \le 10^6$, Time Limit $1.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination**: We must output an answer for *every* prefix $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ in $O(1)$ amortized time per prefix. Enumerating divisors (`Ch 01` SPF sieve) or walking `slink` chains (`Ch 02` $O(\log N)$) is neither necessary nor optimal when a single quotient inequality on the minimum weak period $p_{\min}(i) = i - \pi[i]$ suffices.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Notice what $(AB)^K A$ means in terms of periodicity: let $p = |AB|$ and $r = |A| = i - K p$. Then $0 \le r \le p$ (since $|B| = p - r \ge 0$), $i = K p + r$, and the prefix $S[1..i]$ has **weak period $p$** because shifting $(AB)^K A$ by $p = |AB|$ matches the remaining $(AB)^{K-1} A$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
A prefix $S[1..i]$ can be written as $(AB)^K A$ with $|AB| = p \ge 1$ if and only if there exists a weak period $p \in \operatorname{Per}(S[1..i])$ such that:
$$K \cdot p \le i \le (K + 1) \cdot p.$$
If $K = 1$, this holds for every $i \ge 1$ (take $A = \varepsilon, B = S[1..i]$).
For $K \ge 2$, any $p$ satisfying $K p \le i$ automatically obeys $p \le i / 2$. By the **Half-Length Single-AP Theorem (`Ch 02` Theorem 2.1 / Weak Periodicity Lemma)**, every period $p \in \operatorname{Per}(S[1..i])$ with $p \le i / 2$ is an **exact multiple** of the minimum period $p_{\min} = i - \pi[i]$:
$$p = c \cdot p_{\min} \quad \text{for some integer } c \ge 1.$$
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Substitute $p = c \cdot p_{\min}$ into $K p \le i \le (K + 1) p$:
   $$c K \cdot p_{\min} \le i \le c (K + 1) \cdot p_{\min}.$$

2. Let $q = \lfloor i / p_{\min} \rfloor$ be the number of full minimum-period blocks inside $S[1..i]$. Since we want $c K \cdot p_{\min} \le i$, the largest integer $c$ satisfying $c K \le q$ is:
   $$c = \left\lfloor \frac{\lfloor i / p_{\min} \rfloor}{K} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{i}{K \cdot p_{\min}} \right\rfloor.$$

3. Check in $O(1)$ time whether this largest $c \ge 1$ satisfies the upper bound $i \le c(K + 1) p_{\min}$, i.e., $i - c K p_{\min} \le c p_{\min}$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-I-02"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 1](../chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) & [Chapter 2](../chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd) (`T-1A-01` / `T-1A-02`: Period–Border Duality & Half-Length Period Divisibility · `CF 526D — Om Nom and Necklace`)**.
- **Why Only the Single Largest Multiple $c = \lfloor i / (K p_{\min}) \rfloor$ Needs to Be Checked**:
  Suppose some $c' \ge 1$ satisfies $c' K p_{\min} \le i \le c' (K + 1) p_{\min}$. Since $c' K \le \lfloor i / p_{\min} \rfloor$, we have $c' \le \lfloor i / (K p_{\min}) \rfloor = c$. Because $c \ge c'$ still satisfies $c K p_{\min} \le i$ while making the right-hand bound $c(K + 1) p_{\min}$ *as large as possible*, a valid $c'$ exists if and only if $c = \lfloor i / (K p_{\min}) \rfloor \ge 1$ satisfies $i \le c(K + 1) p_{\min}$!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-1A-02`)**:
  - **Splitting into $p_{\min} \mid i$ vs. $p_{\min} \nmid i$ with Buggy Remainder Checks**: Many contestants try to test $q \bmod K \le q / K$ on $q = i / p_{\min}$ without accounting for the fractional tail $i \bmod p_{\min}$: when $i \bmod p_{\min} > 0$, the remaining tail $A$ must have length $i - c K p_{\min} \le c p_{\min}$ (and when $i - c K p_{\min} = c p_{\min}$, $B$ is empty, which is valid!). Using the single exact inequality `c >= 1 && i - 1LL * c * K * p_min <= 1LL * c * p_min` handles both exact and weak periods uniformly.
- **Complexity**: $O(N)$ time and $O(N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-I-03` — Dual-Lock Periodic Word Synthesis

A communication protocol specifies a message $W[1..N]$ of length $N$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$ of size $\sigma$ ($2 \le \sigma \le 10^9$). You are given a reference framing template $T[1..M]$ ($2 \le M \le 5 \times 10^5$) and $Q$ independent synthesis queries ($1 \le Q \le 2 \times 10^5$).

In each query, you are given two distinct non-empty border lengths $b_1, b_2 \in \operatorname{Border}(T)$ of the reference template $T$ and a target message length $N$ ($1 \le N \le 10^{18}$). A message $W[1..N] \in \Sigma^N$ is **dual-lock compliant** if it simultaneously satisfies both overlap shift equations transferred from $T$:
$$W[i] = W[i + (M - b_1)] \quad (\forall\, 1 \le i \le N - (M - b_1)) \qquad \text{and} \qquad W[i] = W[i + (M - b_2)] \quad (\forall\, 1 \le i \le N - (M - b_2)).$$
(Notice that $W$ does **not** need to contain $T$; it only inherits the two period lengths $p_1 = M - b_1$ and $p_2 = M - b_2$!)

For each query $(b_1, b_2, N)$, verify first that $b_1, b_2 \in \operatorname{Border}(T)$ (output `0` if either is not a valid border of $T$), and otherwise compute the number of dual-lock compliant messages $W[1..N] \in \Sigma^N$ modulo $10^9 + 7$.

- **Constraints**: $2 \le M \le 5 \times 10^5$, $1 \le Q \le 2 \times 10^5$, $1 \le b_1, b_2 < M$, $1 \le N \le 10^{18}$, $2 \le \sigma \le 10^9$, Time Limit $1.5\text{ s}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 01` vs. `Ch 03` Decoy Pair)**: At first glance, seeing borders of $T$, period weights $p_k = M - b_k$, and a huge length $N \le 10^{18}$ looks identical to a `Ch 03` Border-Group Modulo Shortest Path problem (`[WC2016]`). **Do not fall for the decoy!** Here, $W[1..N]$ is a *single* string of length $N$ on which $p_1 = M - b_1$ and $p_2 = M - b_2$ act **simultaneously** across the entire domain $[1, N]$. This is a **`Ch 01` Fine–Wilf Periodicity & Sub-Threshold Orbit Counting** problem!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Each character equality $W[i] = W[i + p_1]$ and $W[i] = W[i + p_2]$ links indices $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ into connected components (character orbits). If there are $C(N; p_1, p_2)$ connected components on $\{1, \dots, N\}$, the number of valid strings is $\sigma^{C(N; p_1, p_2)} \bmod (10^9 + 7)$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Without loss of generality, order the two periods as $1 \le p < q < M$, where $p = \min(M - b_1, M - b_2)$ and $q = \max(M - b_1, M - b_2)$, and let $g = \gcd(p, q)$. By the **Four-Regime Fine–Wilf Orbit Classification (`Ch 01` Theorem 1.2 & Theorem 1.3)**, the exact number of connected components $C(N; p, q)$ on $\{1, \dots, N\}$ is:
$$C(N; p, q) = \begin{cases}
N & \text{if } 1 \le N \le p \quad (\text{neither period creates any edge}), \\
p & \text{if } p < N \le q \quad (\text{only period } p \text{ acts, leaving } p \text{ residue classes}), \\
p + q - N & \text{if } q < N < p + q - g \quad (\text{Sub-Threshold Orbit Formula: } p + q - N \text{ orbits}), \\
g & \text{if } N \ge p + q - g \quad (\text{Above Fine–Wilf Threshold: collapses to period } g = \gcd(p, q)).
\end{cases}$$
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Precompute the KMP array $\pi[1..M]$ of $T$, and walk the fail chain $u = \pi[M], \pi[\pi[M]], \dots$ down to $0$, marking `is_border[u] = true` in $O(M)$ time.
2. For each query $(b_1, b_2, N)$:
   - If `!is_border[b1] || !is_border[b2]`, output `0`.
   - Set $p = \min(M - b_1, M - b_2)$, $q = \max(M - b_1, M - b_2)$, and $g = \gcd(p, q)$.
   - Evaluate $C(N; p, q)$ in $O(1)$ time using the four-way piecewise formula above.
   - Output $\sigma^{C(N; p, q)} \bmod (10^9 + 7)$ via binary exponentiation (reducing the exponent $C(N; p, q) \bmod (10^9 + 6)$ only when $N \le p$ can exceed $10^9 + 6$, since $\sigma \bmod (10^9+7) \ne 0$).
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-I-03"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 1](../chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) (`T-1A-01`: Fine–Wilf Theorem & Sub-Threshold Exact Orbit Formula)**.
- **Why the Sub-Threshold Formula $C(N; p, q) = p + q - N$ Holds (`Ch 01` Return-Map Proof)**:
  For $q \le N < p + q - g$, every vertex $x \in \{q + 1, \dots, N\}$ connects via $-q$ to a unique representative in $\{1, \dots, q\}$. On $\{1, \dots, q\}$, the induced first-return map $\psi(x) = ((x + p - 1) \bmod q) + 1$ decomposes $\{1, \dots, q\}$ into $g = \gcd(p, q)$ directed cycles of length $q / g$. An edge $x \to \psi(x)$ is present in the graph on $\{1, \dots, N\}$ iff $x + p \le N$, which fails for the $k = q - (N - p) = p + q - N$ indices $x \in \{N - p + 1, \dots, q\}$. Because $N < p + q - g \implies k > g$, at least one edge is deleted from each of the $g$ cycles (so zero cycles remain!), turning the $q$ vertices and $q - k$ remaining edges into a forest of $q - (q - k) = k = p + q - N$ trees!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-1A-01`)**:
  - **Using Threshold $p + q$ Instead of $p + q - \gcd(p, q)$**: For $(p, q) = (4, 6)$ and $N = 8 = 4 + 6 - \gcd(4, 6)$, the threshold $p + q - g = 8$ is already reached, so $C(8; 4, 6) = \gcd(4, 6) = 2$. Using $p + q = 10$ would falsely evaluate $p + q - N$ or misclassify $N = 8, 9$.
  - **Forgetting the Regime $p < N \le q$**: When $N < q$, the formula $p + q - N$ gives a number strictly larger than $p$, which is wrong because period $q$ has zero active edges when $N \le q$; the component count is simply $\min(N, p)$.
- **Complexity**: $O(M + Q \log M)$ time and $O(M)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-I-04` — Penalty-Minimized Overlapping Carrier Amplification

A signal repeater starts with a single copy of a base waveform $S[1..N]$ ($2 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$) of initial length $L = N$ and initial penalty $C = 0$. In each amplification step, you may append another copy of $S$ that overlaps the current suffix of the signal by any **positive border** $b \in \operatorname{Border}(S) \setminus \{0\}$ (so $1 \le b \le \pi[N]$):

- This step increases the total signal length by $\Delta L = N - b$;
- Whenever you use a border $b$ that is **strictly shorter** than the maximum border within its own constant-step border group—more concretely, in any arithmetic progression of borders $b_0 > b_1 > \dots > b_c$ with constant step $d$, choosing the $j$-th border $b_j = b_0 - j \cdot d$ adds a phase-drift penalty of $+\alpha \cdot j$ (where $\alpha \ge 0$ is a given integer constant) in addition to increasing length by $x + j \cdot d$ ($x = N - b_0$).

Given a target length threshold $W$ ($N \le W \le 10^{18}$) and a remainder $r_0 \in \{0, 1, \dots, p_{\min} - 1\}$ (where $p_{\min} = N - \pi[N]$ is the shortest period of $S$), find the **minimum possible total length $L_{\min} \ge N$** such that $L_{\min} \equiv r_0 \pmod{p_{\min}}$ and $L_{\min}$ can be generated by zero or more positive-border overlaps; and when $\alpha > 0$, also find the minimum possible combined cost (total length plus total phase-drift penalty) among all valid signals whose length is $\equiv r_0 \pmod{p_{\min}}$.

- **Constraints**: $2 \le N \le 5 \times 10^5$, $N \le W \le 10^{18}$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 03` vs. `Ch 01` Decoy Pair)**: Unlike `CP-I-03` (where periods act simultaneously on one string and collapse via $\gcd$), here each step **sequentially adds** a period weight $p_t = N - b_t$ to the total length $L = N + \sum_t (N - b_t)$. You cannot replace $\{N - b\}$ by their $\gcd$ without paying the Frobenius reachability cost! This is a **`Ch 03` Border-Group Modulo Shortest Path (`T-1A-03`)** problem.
- **Diagnostic Signal**: The set of available positive borders $b \in \operatorname{Border}(S) \setminus \{0\}$ has size up to $N - 1$, which would take $\Theta(N^2)$ in a naive Dijkstra/Bellman-Ford modulo $p_{\min}$. By `Ch 02`, these borders partition into $K \le \lceil \log_2 N \rceil$ arithmetic progressions $\mathcal{A}_k = \{x_k + j \cdot d_k \mid 0 \le j \le c_k\}$. Furthermore, because **only positive borders $b \ge 1$** are allowed (zero-overlap $+N$ is *forbidden* unless $0$ is included!), the initial DP state at the first AP block $(x_1, d_1, c_1)$ must start at modulus $m = x_1$ with $D[N \bmod x_1] = N$ rather than modulus $N$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Walk $u = \pi[N]$ down via $u \leftarrow \operatorname{slink}[u]$ while $u > 0$. Each half-open chain $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ yields a period progression:
$$\mathcal{A}_k = \bigl\{x_k + j \cdot d_k \;\big|\; 0 \le j \le c_k\bigr\}, \qquad x_k = N - \operatorname{len}[u], \quad d_k = \operatorname{diff}[u], \quad c_k = \frac{\operatorname{len}[u] - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]]}{d_k} - 1.$$
When the DP modulus is switched to $x_k$:

1. The base period $x_k \equiv 0 \pmod{x_k}$ shifts the residue by $0$ and is available in unlimited copies.
2. Along each of the $\gcd(d_k, x_k)$ directed cycles of step $+d_k \pmod{x_k}$, unrolling the cycle from its argmin $v_0 = \arg\min D[v]$ as $v_t = (v_0 + t \cdot d_k) \bmod x_k$ yields the bounded-window transition ($1 \le j = t - s \le c_k$):
   $$D[v_t] \leftarrow \min_{t - c_k \le s \le t - 1} \Bigl(D[v_s] + x_k + (t - s) d_k\Bigr) = x_k + t \cdot d_k + \min_{t - c_k \le s \le t - 1} \bigl(D[v_s] - s \cdot d_k\bigr).$$
   If each step $j = t - s$ also incurs penalty $+\alpha \cdot j$, the weight is $x_k + (t - s)(d_k + \alpha)$, so simply replace $d_k$ by $d_k + \alpha$ inside the separated key $D[v_s] - s \cdot (d_k + \alpha)$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Extract the $K \le \lceil \log_2 N \rceil$ AP blocks $(x_k, d_k, c_k)$ from $u = \pi[N]$ down to $u > 0$ (stopping before $u = 0$ because $b = 0$ is disallowed).
2. Reverse or process the blocks so that the final modulus is $x_1 = p_{\min} = N - \pi[N]$ (or switch from the final $m$ to $p_{\min}$ at the end):
   - Initialize $m = x_{\text{first}}$, $D[0..m-1] = +\infty$, and $D[N \bmod m] = N$.
   - For each block $(x_k, d_k, c_k)$, run **Subroutine A (Modulus Switch $m \to x_k$)** via $\gcd(m, x_k)$ cycles starting at each cycle's argmin, followed by **Subroutine B (Monotonic Queue of width $c_k$)** on each $+d_k \pmod{x_k}$ cycle starting at its argmin.
3. Since the first AP block has $x_1 = p_{\min}$ (if processed in reverse order from shortest borders to longest borders, ending at $x_1 = p_{\min}$), the final array $D[r_0]$ directly gives the minimum achievable length $\equiv r_0 \pmod{p_{\min}}$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-I-04"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 3](../chapters/ch03-border-modulo-shortest-path.qmd) (`T-1A-03`: Border-Group Modulo Shortest Path & Residue-Cycle Monotonic Queue)**.
- **Subtlety — Forbidding $b = 0$ (`+N` Transitions) & Processing Order**:
  In standard `[WC2016] 论战捆竹竿`, $b = 0$ (appending $S$ with zero overlap, weight $+N$) is allowed, so we can initialize $m = N$ with $D[0] = N$ (which implicitly makes $+N$ free!). Here, **only positive borders $b \ge 1$** are permitted. If we initialized $m = N$ and later ran Subroutine A with $+N$ transitions, we would illegally allow $b = 0$ overlaps!
  Instead, initialize directly at the first AP's modulus $m = x_{\text{init}}$ with $D[N \bmod x_{\text{init}}] = N$ (which only allows $+x_{\text{init}}$ transitions, and $x_{\text{init}} = N - b_{\text{init}}$ is a valid positive border!). Moreover, by processing the AP blocks from smallest borders to largest borders so that the **last** AP block processed is the top chain $(x_1 = p_{\min}, d_1, c_1)$, the final modulus in memory is automatically $m = p_{\min}$!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-1A-04a`, `BP-1A-04b`)**:
  - **Unbounded vs. 0-1 Deque Push Order (`BP-1A-04b`)**: Inside Subroutine B, you **must** update `D[u] = min(D[u], dq.front().second + x + 1LL * t * d)` *before* computing `key = D[u] - 1LL * t * d` and pushing `(t, key)` into `dq`. Pushing the old `D[u]` before updating restricts the pass to using at most one border from $\mathcal{A}_k$, failing whenever the optimal path uses two borders $x_k + j_1 d_k$ and $x_k + j_2 d_k$ from the same AP block.
  - **Argmin Cycle Rotation (`BP-1A-04a`)**: Always locate `best = argmin D[v]` on each $+d_k \pmod{x_k}$ cycle before starting the sliding window at `t = 0, u = best`.
- **Complexity**: $\sum_{k=1}^K O(x_k) = O(N \log N)$ time and $O(N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-I-05` — Internal Substring Self-Overlap Queries

You are given a string $S[1..N]$ of lowercase English letters ($1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$) and $Q$ independent substring queries ($1 \le Q \le 2 \times 10^5$). Each query specifies an interval $[l, r]$ ($1 \le l \le r \le N$) and asks for the length of the **longest proper border** of the substring $S[l..r]$—that is, the largest integer $b \in \{0, 1, \dots, r - l\}$ such that:
$$S[l .. l + b - 1] = S[r - b + 1 .. r].$$

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N, Q \le 2 \times 10^5$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $512\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination**: Standard KMP only computes borders of **prefixes** $S[1..r]$, and `[POI 2012] A Horrible Poem` (`Ch 01`) only tests **exact periods** $d \mid (r - l + 1)$. Here, the longest border $b$ of $S[l..r]$ corresponds to the shortest **weak period** $p = (r - l + 1) - b$, which need not divide $r - l + 1$ and can be smaller than $(r - l + 1)/2$ (where $b$ is short!).
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Partition the candidate border lengths $b \in [1, r - l]$ of $S[l..r]$ into $\lceil \log_2(r - l + 1) \rceil$ **dyadic scales** $b \in [2^{k-1}, \min(r - l, 2^k - 1)]$. In scale $k$, any valid border $b \in [2^{k-1}, 2^k)$ of $S[l..r]$ must have the prefix $P_k = S[l .. l + 2^{k-1} - 1]$ occurring inside the suffix $T_k = S[r - \min(r-l, 2^k-1) + 1 .. r]$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Look closely at the lengths of $P_k$ and $T_k$ in scale $k$:
$$|P_k| = 2^{k-1}, \qquad |T_k| < 2^k = 2 |P_k|.$$
Because the text window $T_k$ is less than **twice** the length of the pattern $P_k$, any two occurrences of $P_k$ inside $T_k$ overlap by at least $1$ character! By the **Half-Length Single-AP Theorem (`Ch 02` Theorem 2.1 / Internal Pattern Matching Invariant)**:

> The starting positions of all occurrences of a pattern $P$ of length $2^{k-1}$ inside any substring $T$ of length $< 2^k$ form a **single arithmetic progression** (of size $0, 1, 2$, or $\ge 3$ with step $p_{\min}(P)$)!

Conversely, symmetric to occurrences of $P_k$ in $T_k$, every valid border $b \in [2^{k-1}, 2^k)$ also corresponds to an occurrence of the suffix $Q_k = S[r - 2^{k-1} + 1 .. r]$ inside the prefix $S[l .. l + 2^k - 2]$. Intersecting these two arithmetic progressions (one in prefix coordinates, one in suffix coordinates) takes $O(1)$ time per scale $k$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
You can assemble the solution via either of the two canonical `Ch 02` substring-border architectures:

- **Architecture A (Dyadic Weak Periodicity / IPM in $O((N + Q) \log N)$)**:
  - Using Suffix Array + RMQ (or sparse-table doubling equivalence classes on $S$ at lengths $2^k$), for each scale $k = \lfloor \log_2(r-l) \rfloor$ down to $0$:
  - Find the first two and last occurrences of $P_k = S[l .. l + 2^{k-1} - 1]$ inside $S[\max(l+1, r - 2^k + 2) .. r - 2^{k-1} + 1]$ (which have $\operatorname{LCP}(l, pos) \ge 2^{k-1}$, a contiguous range in the Suffix Array queried via persistent segment tree), forming an AP of candidate border lengths $b$, and verify the remaining tail via a single $O(1)$ LCP query (or intersect with the symmetric suffix AP of $Q_k$).
- **Architecture B (Suffix Automaton / Suffix Tree Link-Tree HLD + 2D Range Search in $O((N + Q) \log^2 N)$)**:
  - An index $i \in [l, r - 1]$ defines a valid border $S[l..i]$ of $S[l..r]$ iff $\operatorname{LCSuffix}(S[1..r], S[1..i]) \ge i - l + 1$, i.e., $i - \operatorname{len}(\operatorname{LCA}(u_r, u_i)) \le l - 1$ on the SAM link tree. Decompose the root-to-$u_r$ path into $O(\log N)$ heavy chains and query segment trees over `[l, r - 1]` for the largest $i$ satisfying $i - \operatorname{len}(w) \le l - 1$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-I-05"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 2](../chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd) (`T-1A-02`: Weak Periodicity Lemma, Dyadic Border APs & Substring Border Extraction · `[BJWC 2018] Border 的四种求法` / `Luogu P4482`)**.
- **Why Intersecting the Prefix-Occurrence AP and Suffix-Occurrence AP Avoids Tail Verification**:
  Suppose $b \in [2^{k-1}, 2^k)$ is sought. Write $S[l..l+b-1]$ as the union of its head $P_k = S[l..l+2^{k-1}-1]$ (of length $2^{k-1}$) and its tail $S[l+b-2^{k-1}..l+b-1]$ (of length $2^{k-1}$). Simultaneously, write $S[r-b+1..r]$ as the union of its head $S[r-b+1..r-b+2^{k-1}]$ and its tail $Q_k = S[r-2^{k-1}+1..r]$.
  Then $S[l..l+b-1] = S[r-b+1..r]$ holds **if and only if**:

  1. $P_k = S[l..l+2^{k-1}-1]$ occurs starting at $r - b + 1$ (which restricts $b$ to a single AP $\mathcal{A}_{\text{pref}} \subseteq [2^{k-1}, 2^k)$), **and**
  2. $Q_k = S[r-2^{k-1}+1..r]$ occurs ending at $l + b - 1$ (which restricts $b$ to a single AP $\mathcal{A}_{\text{suff}} \subseteq [2^{k-1}, 2^k)$)!
  Moreover, if $|\mathcal{A}_{\text{pref}}| \ge 3$ and $|\mathcal{A}_{\text{suff}}| \ge 3$ overlap, they share the **exact same common difference** $d = p_{\min}(P_k) = p_{\min}(Q_k)$, making their intersection trivial in $O(1)$ time!

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-1A-03`)**:
  - **Forgetting to Exclude the Improper Border $b = r - l + 1$**: In both the dyadic IPM search and the SAM HLD range search, you must restrict candidate border lengths to $b \le r - l$ (equivalently, right endpoint $i \in [l, r - 1]$). Allowing $i = r$ returns the full substring length $r - l + 1$.
- **Complexity**: $O((N + Q) \log N)$ via Dyadic IPM or $O((N + Q) \log^2 N)$ via SAM Link-Tree HLD.
::::

### Problem `CP-I-06` — Online Prefix-Append Bottleneck Border Stream

You are given an initially empty string $S$ and an initially empty weight array $W$. Over $N$ online steps ($1 \le N \le 3 \times 10^5$), step $i$ appends a lowercase character $c_i$ to $S[1..i]$ and a non-negative integer weight $w_i$ to $W[1..i]$. To enforce strictly online execution, the raw inputs $(c_i', w_i')$ at step $i$ are encrypted using the total answer $\text{ Ans}_{i-1}$ from step $i - 1$.

At step $i$, let $\mathcal{B}^+(i) = (\operatorname{Border}(S[1..i]) \setminus \{0\}) \cup \{i\}$ be the set of all non-empty border lengths of $S[1..i]$ (including the full prefix length $i$ itself). Each $b \in \mathcal{B}^+(i)$ corresponds to the suffix $S[i - b + 1 .. i]$ of length $b$, and its **bottleneck capacity** is the minimum weight inside that suffix combined with an affine position offset:
$$\operatorname{cost}(i, b) = \min_{i - b + 1 \le k \le i} W[k].$$
After each step $i = 1, \dots, N$, compute the cumulative active-border bottleneck sum:
$$\text{Ans}_i = \text{Ans}_{i-1} + \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}^+(i)} \operatorname{cost}(i, b).$$

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 3 \times 10^5$, $0 \le w_i \le 10^9$, Online Encrypted Queries, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 02` vs. `Ch 04` Decoy Pair)**: Because we sum over all borders of $S[1..i]$ at each step $i$, it is tempting to reach for `Ch 04`'s `slink` DP accumulator `g[u] = dp[r - len[slink[u]] - d] + g[fail[u]]`. **Why does `g[u]` fail here?** Because the summand $\operatorname{cost}(i, b) = \min_{k \in [i - b + 1, i]} W[k]$ is **not** a fixed function of the left endpoint $l = i - b + 1$! Every time a small weight $W[i]$ arrives at the right endpoint $i$, it simultaneously truncates $\min_{k \in [l, i]} W[k]$ to $W[i]$ for *every* active left endpoint $l \le i$ whose previous minimum exceeded $W[i]$!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: Instead of grouping borders by `g[u]`, track the set of **currently surviving borders** explicitly across $i - 1 \to i$. When $S[i]$ arrives:
  1. Every surviving proper border $b \in \operatorname{Border}(S[1..i]) \setminus \{0\}$ of $S[1..i]$ is equal to $u + 1$ for some $u \in \operatorname{Border}(S[1..i-1])$ that satisfies **$S[u + 1] = S[i]$**.
  2. Any border $u$ of $S[1..i-1]$ with $S[u + 1] \ne S[i]$ **permanently dies** at step $i$ and never returns! Since at most one new border is born per step, at most $N$ border deaths can ever occur across all $N$ steps—provided we skip surviving borders ($S[u+1] = S[i]$) in $O(1)$ time!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Define the **Next-Character Mismatch Shortcut Link (`Ch 02` Section 3.1 / Theorem 2.4)** on the KMP tree of $S$:
$$\operatorname{anc}[u] = \begin{cases}
\operatorname{anc}[\pi[u]] & \text{if } \pi[u] > 0 \text{ and } S[\pi[u] + 1] = S[u + 1], \\
\pi[u] & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}$$
Notice that $\operatorname{anc}[u]$ depends *only* on $S[1..u+1]$, so $\operatorname{anc}[i - 1]$ can be finalized at step $i$ as soon as $S[i]$ arrives!
When walking down from $u = \pi[i - 1]$ at step $i$:

- If $S[u + 1] \ne S[i]$, then border $u$ **dies** at step $i$; we delete it from our active data structure and step to $u \leftarrow \pi[u]$.
- If $S[u + 1] = S[i]$, then border $u$ **survives** (extending to $u + 1$); we do **not** touch it, and we jump directly to $u \leftarrow \operatorname{anc}[u]$, which is the highest ancestor $v$ of $u$ with $S[v + 1] \ne S[u + 1] = S[i]$ (so $v$ is guaranteed to **die** at step $i$)!
Thus every step of the walk visits a border that dies at step $i$, giving $O(N)$ total visits across the entire run!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}

1. Maintain the active proper borders by their **fixed left endpoints** $l = i - b + 1$ (note that if a border $u$ of $S[1..i-1]$ starts at left endpoint $l = (i-1) - u + 1 = i - u$ and extends to $u + 1$ at step $i$, its left endpoint $l = i - (u + 1) + 1 = i - u$ is **100% invariant**!).
2. Since $\min_{k \in [l, i]} W[k]$ is a step function on $l \in [1, i]$ (governed by a standard monotonic stack on $W$), store the active border counts grouped by their current minimum value $v = \min_{k \in [l, i]} W[k]$ in a frequency map `cnt_by_val[v]`, along with a running `active_sum`.
3. At step $i$:
   - Compute $\pi[i]$ and finalize $\operatorname{anc}[i - 1]$ (since $S[i]$ is now known).
   - Walk $u = \pi[i - 1]$ down to $0$ using $\operatorname{anc}[u]$ to skip survivors; for each dead border $u$ (at left endpoint $l = i - u$), look up its current suffix minimum $\min_{k \in [l, i-1]} W[k]$ via binary search on the monotonic stack of $W$, and decrement `cnt_by_val` and `active_sum`.
   - If $S[1] = S[i]$, insert the newly born length-$1$ border at left endpoint $l = i$ with initial value $W[i-1]$ (before clamping by $W[i]$).
   - Push $W[i]$ onto the monotonic stack and clamp all map entries with key $> W[i]$ down to $W[i]$ in amortized $O(\log N)$ time.
   - Add `active_sum + W[i]` (where $+W[i]$ accounts for the full-length border $b = i$, which always has minimum $\min_{k \in [1, i]} W[k]$, or include $l = 1$ permanently if $b = i$ is tracked).
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-I-06"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 2](../chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd) (`T-1A-02`: Shortcut Link `anc[u]` vs. `slink[u]` Coarsening & Amortized Active-Border Deletion)**.
- **Proof of $O(N)$ Amortized Border Deletions via `anc[u]`**:
  At step $i$, let $u$ be the current node in the fail chain of $i - 1$. If $S[u + 1] \ne S[i]$, node $u$ is deleted from the active set and we advance to $\pi[u]$ (charging $O(1)$ to the death of $u$). If $S[u + 1] = S[i]$, jumping to $v = \operatorname{anc}[u]$ lands on either $0$ or an ancestor $v$ satisfying $S[v + 1] \ne S[u + 1] = S[i]$. In the latter case, $S[v + 1] \ne S[i]$, so $v$ itself **dies at step $i$**! Therefore, every single iteration of the loop (except at most the first check at $\pi[i-1]$ and the termination at $0$) deletes one active border. Since at most $1$ proper border (of length $1$, starting at $l = i$) is inserted at each step $i$, the total number of deletions over $N$ steps is at most $N$.

- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-1A-08`)**:
  - **Computing `anc[i]` Before $S[i+1]$ Arrives**: Because $\operatorname{anc}[u]$ tests whether $S[\pi[u] + 1] = S[u + 1]$, you can only compute $\operatorname{anc}[i - 1]$ at the beginning of step $i$ (once $S[i]$ has been decrypted!). Never access $\operatorname{anc}[i]$ during step $i$.
  - **128-Bit Integer Overflow**: With $N = 3 \times 10^5$ and $w_i = 10^9$, $\text{Ans}_N$ can reach $\frac{1}{2} N^2 \cdot 10^9 \approx 4.5 \times 10^{19} > 2^{64} - 1$. You **must** accumulate $\text{Ans}_i$ in `unsigned __int128` (or `__int128`) and print it with a custom base-$10$ formatter.
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log N)$ time and $O(N)$ space.
::::

### Problem `CP-I-07` — Range-Coupled Palindromic Factorization

You are given a string $S[1..N]$ of lowercase letters ($1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$), an array of threshold positions $L[1..N]$ ($0 \le L[r] < r$), and a penalty weight $C[1..N]$ ($-10^9 \le C[r] \le 10^9$). We wish to partition prefixes of $S$ into palindromic blocks:

- Start with $dp[0] = 0$.
- For each right endpoint $r = 1, 2, \dots, N$ in order:
  1. First, before computing $dp[r]$, every earlier partition state $dp[i]$ residing in the prefix range $0 \le i \le L[r]$ receives an additive bonus $+C[r]$ (i.e., $dp[i] \leftarrow dp[i] + C[r]$ for all $0 \le i \le L[r]$).
  2. Next, $dp[r]$ is set to the **maximum** of the current (updated) values $dp[r - \ell]$ over all lengths $\ell$ such that $S[r - \ell + 1 .. r]$ is a palindrome:
     $$dp[r] = \max_{\substack{1 \le \ell \le r \\ S[r-\ell+1..r] \text{ is a palindrome}}} dp[r - \ell].$$

Compute the final array $dp[1..N]$.

- **Constraints**: $1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5$, $0 \le L[r] < r$, $-10^9 \le C[r] \le 10^9$, Time Limit $2.0\text{ s}$, Memory Limit $256\text{ MB}$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Elimination"}

- **Decoy Elimination (`Ch 04` vs. `Ch 02` Decoy Pair)**: Compare this carefully against `CP-I-06`:
  - Here, we are transitioning over **all palindromic suffixes** $\ell \in \operatorname{PalSuffix}(S[1..r])$, not prefixes/borders of $S[1..r]$ where mismatched suffixes permanently die. A palindromic suffix that disappears at $r$ can reappear at $r + d$! Thus `Ch 02`'s permanent-death argument (`anc[u]`) does **not** apply.
  - Instead, this is a **`Ch 04` Series-Link (`slink`) Left-Endpoint Shift-Overlap DP (`T-1A-04` / `W1A-42`)** coupled with range updates on the left-endpoint array $dp[0..N]$!
- **Diagnostic Signal**: By `Ch 04` Theorem 4.2 (Shift-Overlap Invariant), for each `slink` chain head $u$ at position $r$ with step $d = \operatorname{diff}[u]$, the set of left endpoints $\mathcal{I}(u, r) = \{r - \ell_1, \dots, r - \ell_k\}$ queried by $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ equals $\mathcal{I}(\operatorname{fail}[u], r - d) \sqcup \{r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - d\}$. Why can't a plain scalar `g[u]` handle step 1's range update $dp[0..L[r]] \mathrel{+}= C[r]$? Because between $r - d$ and $r$, range updates have modified a subset of the left endpoints inside $\mathcal{I}(\operatorname{fail}[u], r - d)$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Combinatorial Word Invariant"}
Look at the structure of the left-endpoint set $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ for any PAM node $u$ with step $d = \operatorname{diff}[u]$:
$$\mathcal{I}(u, r) = \bigl\{\,r - \operatorname{len}[u],\; r - \operatorname{len}[u] + d,\; \dots,\; r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - d\,\bigr\}.$$
Every element $i \in \mathcal{I}(u, r)$ has the **exact same residue modulo $d$**, and as $r$ advances by $+d$, the set $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ simply appends one new element $i_{\text{new}} = r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - d$ at the right end while keeping its leftmost element $i_{\text{old}} = r - \operatorname{len}[u]$ fixed!

Even simpler: to maintain $g[u] = \max_{i \in \mathcal{I}(u, r)} dp[i]$ under range additions $dp[0..L[r]] \mathrel{+}= C[r]$ when arbitrary $d$-APs cannot be grouped in a single standard segment tree, observe how $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ evolves on the **PAM fail tree**:
Whenever $u$ is a `slink` chain head at step $r$, $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ is a contiguous range of indices **within the sequence of left endpoints pushed onto the unique period-$d$ chain containing $u$**!
Specifically, in the PAM fail tree, group nodes into maximal chains of constant $\operatorname{diff}[v] = d$. Along any maximal period-$d$ chain $\mathcal{C}$, each time the chain is visited at a right endpoint $r$, **at most one new left endpoint** $i_{\text{new}} = r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - d$ is appended to $\mathcal{C}$'s list of left endpoints in **strictly increasing order of $i$**!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 3 — Algorithmic & Data-Structure Assembly"}
Because every maximal constant-`diff` chain $\mathcal{C}$ in the PAM fail tree receives new left endpoints $i_{\text{new}} = r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - d$ in **strictly increasing order** (and the active subset $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ for a chain head $u \in \mathcal{C}$ is simply the contiguous suffix of $\mathcal{C}$'s list with $i \ge r - \operatorname{len}[u]$!):

1. Verify whether any element of $\mathcal{C}$'s list is ever $< r - \operatorname{len}[u]$: by `Ch 04` Theorem 4.2, $\mathcal{I}(u, r) = \mathcal{I}(\operatorname{fail}[u], r - d) \sqcup \{i_{\text{new}}\}$, which starts at $r - \operatorname{len}[u]$—the **very first** left endpoint ever inserted into $\mathcal{C}$!
2. Furthermore, to support range add on $i \in [0, L[r]]$ across **all** chains simultaneously in $O(\log N)$ time:
   - Each step $r$ visits $O(\log r)$ `slink` chains and inserts $O(\log r)$ pairs $(\text{chain\_id}, i_{\text{new}})$.
   - **Three Structural Regimes for Range Updates**:
     - **Case 1 (Additive weight on the palindrome / suffix itself, i.e., updates on PAM fail-tree subtrees or right-endpoint windows)**: A lazy segment tree over the DFS order of the PAM fail tree updates all active palindromic suffixes in $O(\log N)$.
     - **Case 2 (Monotone Frontier / Sliding Window $L[r-1] \le L[r]$)**: When $L[r]$ is non-decreasing ($L[1] \le L[2] \le \dots \le L[N]$), each left endpoint $i$ crosses the frontier $i \le L[r]$ **at most once**! When $i$ crosses $L[r]$, at most $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil$ `slink` chains contain $i$ (the chains visited at step $i + \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] + d$). Updating those $O(\log N)$ chains in a segment tree over PAM nodes takes **$O(N \log^2 N)$** total time!
     - **Case 3 (General $L[r]$ via Period Thresholding)**: For any chain head $u$, $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ has size $k = (\operatorname{len}[u] - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]]) / d$. For $d > B$, $k \le N / B$ elements are queried directly in a global Segment Tree over $i \in [0, N]$; for $d \le B$, ordering a Segment Tree by $(d, i \bmod d, \lfloor i / d \rfloor)$ turns $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ into a **single contiguous interval**!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete Derivation, Complexity Proof & Reference Solution — CP-I-07"}

- **Target Chapter & Technique ID**: **[Chapter 4](../chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd) (`T-1A-04` / `T-1A-05`: PAM `slink` Shift-Overlap Invariant Coupled with Segment Tree / Frontier Activation, `W1A-42`)**.
- **Complete Structural Decomposition**:
  By Theorem 4.2 (`Ch 04`), at right endpoint $r$, the half-open `slink` chain $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ queries the exact left-endpoint set:
  $$\mathcal{I}(u, r) = \mathcal{I}(\operatorname{fail}[u], r - d) \sqcup \bigl\{\,i_{\text{new}}(u, r)\,\bigr\}, \qquad i_{\text{new}}(u, r) = r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - \operatorname{diff}[u].$$
  Notice the crucial cardinality bound: at each right endpoint $x \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, the `slink` loop visits at most $\lceil \log_2 x \rceil$ chain heads $u$, and each visit creates **exactly one** new left-endpoint membership $i = x - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - \operatorname{diff}[u]$ in the constant-`diff` chain containing $u$.

  - Therefore, across the entire algorithm, each left endpoint $i \in \{0, \dots, N - 1\}$ belongs to **at most $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil$ constant-`diff` chains** (or, if we maintain a lazy segment tree / monotonic deque over the elements of each constant-`diff` chain indexed by their insertion rank, the total number of leaves across all chains is $\sum_{r=1}^N |\text{chains}(r)| = O(N \log N)$!).
  - When range updates follow a monotone frontier (or sliding window $[L_1[r], L_2[r]]$), each of the $O(N \log N)$ chain leaves enters and leaves the active window at most once, updating its chain's segment-tree/deque accumulator in $O(\log N)$ (or $O(1)$) time, for a total complexity of $O(N \log^2 N)$ (or $O(N \log N)$)!
  - Even for completely arbitrary $L[r]$ without monotonicity, splitting by period threshold $d \le B$ (where $\mathcal{I}(u, r)$ is a contiguous range in the $(d, i \bmod d)$-ordered segment tree) versus $d > B$ (where $|\mathcal{I}(u, r)| \le N / B$ is queried directly) or using `slink` tree paths solves the problem strictly sub-quadratically.
- **Boundary Pitfall Audit (`BP-1A-05`, `BP-1A-06`)**:
  - **The $r - \operatorname{len}[u]$ vs. $r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - \operatorname{diff}[u]$ Trap (`BP-1A-05`)**: The newly entering left endpoint at step $r$ is **always** $i_{\text{new}} = r - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] - \operatorname{diff}[u]$ (the rightmost / shortest palindrome in the half-open chain $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$). The leftmost endpoint $r - \operatorname{len}[u]$ was the very first element inserted into the chain when its bottom node was first visited!
- **Complexity**: $O(N \log N)$ to $O(N \log^2 N)$ time and $O(N \log N)$ space.
::::

| **`BP-1A-03`** | `Ch 02` | Treating $[\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ as a closed interval in sum/counting DPs, or allowing $b = r - l + 1$ in substring border queries (`CP-I-05`). | Since $\operatorname{len}[v_c] - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{slink}[u]] = \operatorname{diff}[u]$, node $\operatorname{slink}[u]$ belongs to the next AP chain. Always use half-open $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$. |
| **`BP-1A-04a`** | `Ch 03` | Starting $+d_k \pmod{x_k}$ residue-cycle relaxation at residue $0$ instead of $v_0 = \arg\min D[v]$ (`CP-I-04`). | Starting at a non-minimum vertex misses shortest paths wrapping past $v_0$. Rotating to $\arg\min D[v]$ unrolls the cycle into a DAG. |
| **`BP-1A-04b`** | `Ch 03` | Pushing old $D[v_t] - t \cdot d_k$ into the monotonic deque *before* updating $D[v_t]$ from `dq.front()` (`CP-I-04`). | Restricts each pass to at most one item from $\mathcal{A}_k$ (0-1 knapsack). Update $D[v_t]$ *first*, then push updated $D[v_t] - t \cdot d_k$. |

Range updates on $dp[0..L[r]]$ require chain-indexed segment trees or frontier activation. |
